text: Another example would be the Enabled Living Programme, where we work with our partners to pilot innovative approaches to empower persons with disabilities to live independently, build meaningful connections and enhance their overall well-being.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In addition, we want to push the envelope and co-create AI and technology solutions that directly enhance the quality of life of our clients.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In my work trips to China and Qatar last year, I was deeply impressed by the adoption of innovative AI solutions and the possibilities they presented to enable persons with disabilities to work, live and play.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For hearing-impaired individuals like Mr Raiyme, who is a desktop engineer at NCS, new technologies coming onstream can be very empowering socially.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For instance, with the real-time transcription and translation capabilities of the LLVision's AI-powered glasses, Raiyme is able to converse better at home with his mom, whom he lipreads in Malay.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: And of course, the AI machine needs to learn Malay better.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: He does not need translation because AI will do it for him.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In Qatar, hologram assistants that can respond to hearing-impaired persons via sign language are installed in public spaces, including public transportation sites.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These technologies may only impact a small proportion of each society, but the impact is profound on the beneficiaries and their families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: And when we collaborate and cooperate with regional partners, it allows us to have greater scale to support the development and adoption of such technology.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For persons with disabilities, SG Enable will continue to champion the responsible use of AI and technology solutions – a topic that is close to Miss Rachel Ong's heart.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: SG Enable will curate more devices to and continue to create more devices for persons with disabilities, including those enhanced by AI capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Under the Enabling Lives Initiative Grant, funding is also provided to support AI solutions that improve independence and expand employment opportunities for persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: One example would be AiSee, an AI-powered wearable device that enables persons with visual impairment to better understand their surroundings through voice prompts.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Beyond the belief that AI and technology takes away jobs, they can in fact be a force for good; enablers that allow us to break new ground both in how we support our professionals and clients.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I am excited by its potential and opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We want better for the clients and families we support: better outcomes, better opportunities, better lives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is what drives our work at MSF.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The way to achieve this is through all of us working together and staying united, especially amidst global uncertainties.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: At MSF, we are making progress with our partners across the social service sector, with corporates, with IHLs, with volunteers and with the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I call on all Singaporeans to join us in this endeavour.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: When we work together, we unlock new possibilities and achieve far better outcomes than what we can accomplish alone.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It is this collective spirit and the willingness of Singaporeans to support and empower one another that drives real and lasting change.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Which is why MSF will soon launch a campaign "Better Starts with Us", because at MSF, we believe it is through this shared commitment that each of us, we are not just building a strong and united society, but a Singapore that is a great place for all families to achieve their goals and aspirations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Chairman, several Members, such as Mr Xie Yao Quan, Mr Melvin Yong, Ms Mariam Jaafar and Mr Cai Yinzhou, have raised concerns about improving social mobility.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: This has always been an area of focus for the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF).

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: As we saw in the Ministry of Finance (MOF) Occasional Paper last month, Singapore has done relatively well in this area compared to other advanced economies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: However, like in other advanced economies, pressures are likely to persist or even intensify.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Hence, MSF will redouble our efforts to enhance social mobility.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: MSF's goal is to support lower-income families to progressively achieve the "3S" outcomes: stability, self-reliance and ultimately, social mobility.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We are going beyond social assistance to social empowerment by supporting our families through three things.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: When families fall on hard times, we provide a safety net through immediate support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: MSF provides a boost so families can get back on their feet and take the next step forward.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: MSF supports families with opportunities to grow their own resources.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Such opportunities, when harnessed, will allow families to reach, grab the next rung and pull themselves up.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: In this way, MSF empowers families to succeed by overcoming challenges, seizing opportunities and most importantly, doing so with dignity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We started with families living in public rental housing and we have been expanding to other lower-income families, such as those on KidSTART.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Each ComLink+ family has a Social Service Office (SSO) family coach or Family Service Centre (FSC) case worker.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: They are the family’s greatest champion – someone in their corner who understands their circumstances and walks alongside them towards their longer-term goals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan suggested efforts to address slowing social mobility.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: ComLink+ seeks to do precisely that by providing targeted support across key domains and over different life stages, such as income security, children’s development and education, housing, family functioning, financial resilience and health.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: As families’ needs are varied and dynamic, we co-develop an action plan with each family.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: As mentioned by Minister Masagos, MSF is committed to invest in research to better understand the impact of these efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We do not have all the answers on how to best support families to achieve social mobility.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: But by learning continuously and applying these insights, we will be able to refine our intervention and update our slate of support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: From a safety net to a steadying hand.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: When family coaches or case workers start journeying with families, they address the families' immediate needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: This could mean referring the family for ComCare assistance and other financial support for some interim relief.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Together, these form our safety net for families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: But a safety net may not be enough for upward mobility.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: This is where we offer a hand to give families a boost to progress in a steady, sustained manner.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We therefore introduced the ComLink+ Progress Packages to encourage families moving towards their goals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Launched progressively over the last two years, these packages boost families’ efforts through financial top-ups when they take action in four areas: preschool enrolment and attendance, employment, debt clearance and home ownership.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Joseph remembers when Mr Suhaimi shared his dream to move out of their rental flat and into their own home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Hearing that, Joseph worked with the family to chart out a roadmap and encouraged them along the way to achieve this dream.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Acting on the plan, both Ms Erna and Mr Suhaimi are working hard.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: They are committed to employment and their children’s education.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: With ComLink+ Progress Package top-ups, they are also able to set aside more savings for their future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: However, as noted by Mr Melvin Yong, some families find the conditions too complicated or difficult to meet.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: It reflects the families' commitment to work with us to improve their circumstances.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Families will receive this payout after agreeing to be on ComLink+ and will continue to receive it so long as they keep taking steps towards their goals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: With steady, predictable support, families can better focus on longer-term goals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Second, many families work hard to maintain employment and regular preschool attendance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Yet, despite genuine effort, some may not be able to meet their targets due to their circumstances.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We are therefore adjusting our conditions to better support families with more complex challenges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: For example, Ms Erna's part-time job's salary currently does not qualify her for payout on its own.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: However, with the enhanced progress package, it will now be counted together with her husband's earnings towards their family's employment milestones.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: For preschool, we will introduce intermediate milestones to encourage families' progress towards regular attendance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: At the same time, a portion will continue to be placed in families' Central Provident Fund (CPF) and Child Development Accounts (CDA), so that we support not just today's needs but also tomorrow's security.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: As noted by Mr Cai Yinzhou, some families may be hesitant to get on board ComLink+.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Together with these enhancements, family coaches will step up efforts to reach out to families by working closely with Government agencies and community partners in their support system.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Once families get back on their feet and start to move forward, we support them to take charge of their long-term progress.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: At MSF, our goal is to create opportunities that families can seize for themselves.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Employment is one of the best ways to do this.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: However, lower-income families often face barriers to employment that are not so straightforward to address, especially with limited financial resources.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: On job matching, MSF is reviewing how to provide tailored support for lower-income families navigating the world of work as they may face more challenges finding suitable jobs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: For example, lower-income jobseekers tend to work in service industries, where work schedules are less flexible on short notice.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: This makes it harder to deal with family emergencies, such as picking their children from school when they fall ill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: MSF is thus working with partners, such as Employment and Employability Institute (e2i), AKG and TOUCH Community Services, to strengthen employment support for these families to prepare them for work, find suitable jobs and ultimately do well in their jobs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We will also provide more support for upskilling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Some ComLink+ families today have younger jobseekers, who with the right skills, can unlock better-paying jobs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: While broad-based schemes like SkillsFuture exist, ComLink+ families may benefit from a more targeted approach.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Families bear some costs when they choose to upskill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: For example, their income may be disrupted during their studies and it is not certain even that they will get a job with a higher salary after.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: On caregiving, parents will have peace of mind to work when they know that their children are being taken care of and meaningfully engaged after school hours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: MSF supports this by making after-school care more accessible, more affordable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We are also giving parents greater assurance of support so that they can plan ahead.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Parents can now submit their Student Care Fee Assistance applications up to six months before their child’s enrolment in a Student Care Centre.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Eligible parents will be granted in-principle approval, which guarantees that they will receive Student Care Fee Assistance once they enrol in an eligible centre.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We are also extending the maximum Student Care Fee Assistance assistance period from 24 months to 36 months.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Mr Cai Yinzhou highlighted that children should have opportunities to continue developing holistically outside school hours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: As a parent myself, the time I spend with my children after hours, after work, allows me to bond with them and explore their interests.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Lower-income families, who are often stretched in time and resources, could especially benefit from additional support to purposefully engage their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: As part of Grow Well SG, we have worked with Families for Life partners to provide low-cost activities for screen-free family bonding.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Families can enjoy children's books, discounted attractions and community events.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Working towards the 3S outcomes is a long journey for our ComLink+ families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: One of the factors that can derail progress is dealing with health issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: When we are unwell, it is not easy to meet our responsibilities at home, at school or at work, let alone pursue our aspirations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: And yet, for many ComLink+ families who are busy making ends meet, they tend to deprioritise these health concerns.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Over time, this can lead to poorer health outcomes, leaving some families trapped in a vicious cycle where poor health makes it harder to stabilise their lives, and life's pressures make it even harder for them to stay well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We want to help them break out of this cycle.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Therefore, as mentioned by Minister Masagos, we trialled a new model of support in 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We tested how family coaches and healthcare staff, together, could achieve two things.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: First, set health goals and actions that support families to take care of their health even as they juggle competing needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Second, streamline service delivery, so families do not have to interact with too many officers, which can be overwhelming.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: MSF, the Ministry of Health and the healthcare clusters are finetuning the model and will extend it to more ComLink+ families this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Together with the extension of Healthier SG to younger ComLink+ families, shared by Minister Masagos, we hope families will be empowered to take charge of their health.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Ms Mariam Jaafar would be pleased to know that as we develop more interventions to support families towards the 3S outcomes, families will not face a navigation nightmare.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Instead, it has always been the intent of ComLink+ for family coaches to co-develop action plans with families that sequence the interventions in a manageable way.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Family coaches will also connect families to the resources and support to achieve their goals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: This is how ComLink+ aims to provide each family with a pathway towards social mobility tailored to their needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Such efforts reveal how we can do better together, but the Government cannot do this alone.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Minister Masagos proposed 3Cs to guide how we partner with others.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We look forward to more partners coming onboard.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: With tighter partnerships, we can weave stronger safety nets, offer more steadying hands and craft sturdier supported ladders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Together, we will journey with our families to achieve stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: (In Malay):   In these challenging times, many Singaporean families face numerous obstacles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: These include rising costs of living, the need to upgrade skills in a rapidly changing economy and various daily responsibilities that often test our families' resilience and perseverance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Yet we continue to stand firm, facing these challenges steadfastly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: As the saying goes, "Effort is the ladder to success".

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Every small step taken with a sharp mind, determination and collaborative spirit brings us closer to our dreams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: With sustained and comprehensive support, their efforts will bear even greater fruit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: In their journey to improve their quality of life, families like Mdm Erna's do not have to go through it alone.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: With this enhanced package, families like Mdm Erna's can better manage daily expenses and build savings for the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Beyond Government support, community organisations play a vital role.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We must stand by those families in need.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We value our Malay/Muslim organisations' efforts and hope more organisations will join hands with MSF to build a caring and united society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Through close cooperation, we can build a caring and inclusive society for everyone at every stage of life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Let us continue working together to build a Singapore that gives hope and opportunities for every family to become stronger, self-reliant and progress.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Strong families are the bedrock of a successful society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: (In English): Chairman, real support is not just once-off.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Families, like Ms Erna's, know their strength and hard work will be seen by their family coaches, like Joseph.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: In MSF, we believe that collective efforts by the Government, partners and the families themselves, will turn obstacles into opportunities, trials into triumphs, hardships into hope for families who need it the most.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: As a society, we need to ensure that no family is trapped by their circumstances, no child is defined by their starting point, no potential goes unrealised and no hope beyond reach.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: This is not just a social policy; it is a moral responsibility.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: As a society, we will empower all families to unlock their maximum potential, for a brighter future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: As we move collectively from assistance to empowerment, this future is shaped not by what we give to families, but by what families are enabled to become.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Chairman, a fair and inclusive society does not expect people to fit neatly into our systems.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Instead, it asks the question: how must our systems evolve so that every person can flourish?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: At MSF, that is the question guiding our work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Earlier, Minister of State Zhulkarnain spoke about uplifting low-income families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: When I meet parents and caregivers, one concern surfaces time and again.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: They ask me, after my child graduates from special education (SPED) school, what comes next?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And most importantly: perhaps when I am no longer around, who will look after my child?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And third, building lifelong security so families can plan with confidence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For many families, graduation from SPED school is both a proud milestone as well as a moment of uncertainty.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Behind each statistic is a young person taking a brave step into adulthood, and parents learning, oftentimes anxiously, to let go.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Access to lifelong learning is important to facilitate a smoother transition to life beyond school.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Ng Chee Meng and Ms Denise Phua will be pleased to know that we provide funding support for skills training through the SG Enable Training Grant.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SG Enable, supported by SkillsFuture Singapore, will introduce new courses from April this year, adding to the existing 140 active courses curated by the Enabling Academy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SG Enable is partnering employers in sectors, such as food and beverage (F&B) and Health and Social services to curate job roles thoughtfully.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And through various grants, wage offsets and the Enabling Mark, our national accreditation framework, organisations can steadily strengthen the inclusive hiring practices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It enriches workplaces with resilience, loyalty and diverse perspectives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For graduates with higher support needs, centre-based services remain critical.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Today, about 3,600 PwDs attend our Daily Activity Centres (DACs) and Sheltered Workshops (SWs).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Behind this number are real families, like 21-year-old Mirza and his mother, Mdm Habibah, who simply wants the best for her son.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: After graduating from SPED school, Mirza tried a placement with a SW before eventually settling into a DAC at SUN-DAC.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For him, the DAC gives him good structure, friendship and a safe space to grow.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Every Thursday, Mirza goes on walks around Bedok.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: He buys prata, sometimes ice cream, learns how to count money and take the bus.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For his mother, Mdm Habibah, the programme gives her peace of mind.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: When the child graduates, six months can feel like an eternity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But in fact, we have already added 100 shelter workshop places in 2024.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As capacity builds, families on the waitlist are not left alone.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Enabling Services Hubs (ESHs) offer activities and serve as community touch points.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For recent graduates, the Supported Transition and Engagement Programme (STEP) ensures they remain meaningfully engage with outings and activities at least twice weekly while waiting for placement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: All this, because transition should not mean isolation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We also heard feedback that moving between SW and DACs can be cumbersome.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Re-assessments, transitions – families told us that it felt like starting from scratch each time the needs changed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: So, last year we launched the Enabling Skills for Life Programme (ESLP).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: ESLP integrates both models – SW and DAC – into a single continuum.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: More importantly, it introduces individualised curriculum and development plans co-created with clients and caregivers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: That co-creation is important because no one knows a person's strengths and aspirations better than the individual himself or herself, and the family members.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our aim is simple: as each individual grows, the support around them grows too.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This means that ESLP clients will have access to more training pathways depending on their specific needs and aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To this end, MSF is piloting two community living models to strengthen support for independent living.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The first is the Enabled Living Programme (ELP) pilot, which has started in five locations, and we are doing this in close partnership with appointed SSAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Delivered within designated public rental flats, ELP allows PwDs with low to moderate support needs and no to little family support to live independently.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: When I recently spoke to Boon Hao, an ELP resident supported by the Autism Resource Centre, he did not talk about policies or subsidies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: He spoke about hosting his friends on Valentine's Day – about the dishes he prepared, about the chore schedule he shares with his roommate, Vincent, about grocery runs at Ang Mo Kio Hub.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These may sound like mundane things, but for Boon Hao, they represent dignity, independence, friendship.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through ELP, persons with low to moderate support needs can live independently in public rental flats, supported by coaches and community networks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Residents may not live with family, but they are never alone.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Grassroots leaders check in, neighbours build friendships, and Boon Hao is even exploring volunteering.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Alongside community-living models, we are strengthening neighbourhood support through our ESHs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The idea is straightforward: support should be close to home and easy to access.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our ESHs in Tampines, Punggol and Jurong have worked with over 300 community partners and volunteers in the past two years: from grassroots organisations to schools and local businesses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: They conduct outreach, organise learning workshops and social activities, and link PwDs and caregivers to relevant services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For families, the ESH can be a reassuring first touchpoint: a place to ask questions, seek guidance and find support without feeling overwhelmed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: More importantly, ESHs help communities grow in confidence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through inclusion workshops and partnerships, neighbours learn how to better welcome and support PwDs in everyday settings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Because when support is embedded within our neighborhoods, PwDs are not seen simply as clients of a programme, but they are recognised as fellow residents, friends and contributors to the same community they live in.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Many worry most not about themselves, but about what will happen after they are gone.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We recognise the challenges they face and we must ensure they are well-supported on this journey.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As Singapore ages, this concern becomes more urgent.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As noted by Assoc Prof Kenneth Poon, a chief area of concern for caregivers is how their loved ones will be cared for after they pass.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We are supporting families in three ways: first, near-term relief; second, strengthened savings; and third, secure future arrangements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: First, to provide near-term financial relief, Prime Minister announced in Budget last year that subsidies will be increased for adult disability services and extended to more households.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Since January this year, subsidies for the Assistive Technology Fund were enhanced, and extended to families with per capita income between $2,601 and $4,800.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through the Assistive Technology Fund, eligible families can purchase assistive technology devices for independent living.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Denise Phua and Ms Kuah Boon Theng would be pleased to know that these enhancements will provide additional financial relief for 3,600 PwDs accessing our residential and community disability services, including those attending Day Activity Centres.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Phua and Ms Kuah also noted that our funding to service providers impact service access and quality.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And that is exactly why we regularly review our funding models for relevance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We last increased funding to Day Activity Centre providers in 2021, and to disability residential service providers last year, in 2025, to account for inflation and enhanced staffing requirements for clients with higher support needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The inter-agency Taskforce on Assurance for Families with Persons with Disabilities will explore more ways to keep disability support affordable for families and sustainable for service providers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This was announced by the Ministry of Manpower at the Committee of Supply last year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Under the MRSS, we dollar-match CPF top-ups for those eligible, up to an annual cap of $2,000 and a lifetime limit of $20,000.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This means that if a parent of a seven-year-old with a verified disability status tops up $2,000 annually to their child's account, we will match by topping up another $2,000 each year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Assuming: one, the parent consistently tops up $2,000 annually over 10 years to hit the lifetime cap of $20,000; and two, a 4% compounding interest, this child would have minimally $320,000 in CPF retirement savings by age 65.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This translates to at least $1,700 in monthly payouts for life, from age 65.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: If a parent tops up consistently from a young age, the compounded impact can be substantial, giving their child meaningful CPF payouts in later life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is all about dignity in their senior years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Caregivers need assurance that these funds are secure when they are no longer around.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As announced at Budget last year, we will be introducing a dollar-for-dollar matching grant for tops-ups to the Special Needs Trust (SNT) accounts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Parents can further multiply their financial provisions for their child by buying a Great Eastern Cares Term Plan.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This term plan insures parents up till age 100, with coverage ranging from $100,000 to $300,000.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For insurance coverage of $250,000, a healthy 33-year-old mother with per capita household income below $3,600 would only need to make a one-off trust top-up of $10,000 to her child's account to cover the total premiums for the plan.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Upon the insured parent's demise before age 100, $250,000 will be paid into the child's SNT account.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As premiums increase with age and the amount insured, caregivers are thus encouraged to start these conversations early with SG Enable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Kitty is the mother of a child living with autism and she was initially hesitant due to the initial capital needed to start an SNT account for her child.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: While we work on ensuring our initiatives remain fit for purpose, we agree with Miss Rachel Ong that raising awareness is a crucial part of ensuring that these initiatives have reach.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Beyond what is available on their website, SG Enable has developed the Enabling Guide to consolidate information on available support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And they will also continue engaging with partners, such as employers and industry chambers, to raise awareness of inclusive hiring and employment support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We also endeavour to improve accessibility to our initiatives given the wide range of needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: There are also SSAs like SADeaf, who provide casework and counselling services using sign language.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Chairman, please allow me to say a few words in Mandarin.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Chairman, promoting a more inclusive Singapore is the shared aspiration of all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We hope to build a Singapore where PwDs can pursue their own ideals and aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through employment support, Day Activity Centres and Sheltered Workshops, as well as the Enabling Skills for Life Programme, we hope to help PwDs build lifelong learning capabilities, enabling them to better integrate into society and live meaningful lives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We implement the Enabled Living Programme, the Home Support Programme, and establish Enabling Services Hubs to strengthen the support networks for persons with disabilities at home and in the community, allowing them to live independently in the community for the long term.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have not forgotten about the family members and caregivers around PwDs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will continue to collaborate with partners from all sectors to ensure that every person with disabilities can find their place in our country and live dignified and meaningful lives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is our commitment and determination in building a more inclusive and caring home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: (In English): Chairman, as we journey towards 2030, our commitment very clear: to build a Singapore where PwDs pursue aspirations with confidence, where families trust that support will endure.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Inclusion happens when employers open doors, when neighbours extend friendship and when communities choose to see ability before disability.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: PwDs are not defined by what they need.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: They are defined by the strengths they contribute: resilience, creativity, loyalty, courage.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: They are not passive recipients of support, much like seniors in our community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: So, let us move forward together: not by asking people to fit into narrow definitions, but by shaping a society heartful enough for every Singaporean to belong.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And that is how we advance an inclusive Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Mr Chairman, MSF is committed to building a nation that supports Singaporeans in raising strong families and giving every child a good start.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Today, I will elaborate on three strategies to achieve this: starting strong – building firm foundations within the home; starting early – ensuring access to affordable and quality early childhood education; and starting together – working as a community to support our families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: And if we take the first letter of each, they spell out SET, reflecting our shared commitment to ensuring that families are set to thrive in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: I will begin by sharing how we are supporting our families to start strong.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: For many of us, families are our safe harbour and where we turn to in our happiest and also our most challenging moments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: An MSF survey in 2023 showed that most Singaporeans have a closely-knit family and believe in its importance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We will continue to support families to build strong foundations within the home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Mr Gabriel Lam and Mr Melvin Yong asked about support available for the different family types, while Ms Eileen Chong asked about strengthening support for parents and caregivers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: MSF is committed in our efforts to strengthen all families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Our children deserve to be valued and given equal opportunities to thrive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Benefits that support their growth and development, such as subsidies for education, healthcare, and the CDA, are given to all citizen children, regardless of their parents’ marital status.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: To help all families stay resilient, we offer holistic support at every stage of life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: These programmes range from financial assistance to family counselling to parenting workshops.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: For more vulnerable households, by adopting a holistic case management approach, our Family Service Centres help them manage multiple stressors and break out of inter-generational patterns.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Minister Masagos has also shared that we will double our family counselling capacity under the Strengthening Families Programme (FAM) by 2030.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: The Ministry of Manpower has also introduced the Tripartite Guidelines on flexible work arrangements to help caregivers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: MSF will continue to track the resilience of families and study whether to provide more targeted support for single parent households.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We also recognise that some children may not have access to stable homes with their biological parents, and may require adoption or fostering.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim and Dr Neo Kok Beng have asked about these arrangements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Today, there are multiple layers of checks in our adoption processes to detect child trafficking.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Singapore has adopted regional frameworks to complement our domestic efforts to protect children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We undertake regular reviews to ensure that our processes, our laws and our international efforts are effective in combating unethical adoption practices and child trafficking.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: In fostering arrangements, we facilitate regular contact or access between children and their biological parents to maintain links, wherever safe and appropriate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We have also seen cases where foster parents proactively help children reunite with their biological parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: MSF remains open to considering ways to facilitate this, including co-parenting, recognising also that every case is unique.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: I would also like to take this opportunity to thank all foster parents, including Dr Neo, for their efforts in providing positive family environments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Members of this House have raised this topic, including Mr Yip Hon Weng, Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Kenneth Tiong.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We encourage all Singaporeans to make their LPA while they are still healthy and to do so as soon as possible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We acknowledge Members' feedback about the challenges faced in the scenarios where individuals require Professional Donees or Deputies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Building a strong family environment requires creating healthy habits and quality time together – a challenge when screens increasingly dominate family life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Mr Cai Yinzhou and Miss Rachel Ong raised valid concerns about prolonged screen usage and exposure to AI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Parents are our first and most important line of defence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: For practical support, I will refer parents to the Infocomm Media Development Authority's (IMDA's) Digital for Life portal and MSF’s Families for Life Parenting website.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: They offer guiding materials on managing children’s screen time, and helping them navigate the online world safely and to use AI responsibly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: By reducing screen times, we hope parents can create opportunities to bond and form meaningful connections with their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Every year, we dedicate the month of June to celebrating families through the month-long National Family Festival (NFF).

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Last year, more than 850,000 participated in activities like family carnivals, games and experiential learning activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: With greater community and corporate support, we hope to welcome one million participants to participate in NFF 2026 this year and to create even more memories as a family.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Through our partnerships, MSF has been bringing more quality and affordable family activities directly to local communities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: These include kite-making, reading programmes, community lo-hei, since Chinese New Year just passed, as well as discounts from commercial partners for family outings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Families can find upcoming events and good discounts on the Families for Life website.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Next, let me touch on Starting Early, I would like to share how we will further enhance our early childhood education.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Research has shown that the early years are crucial to a child’s development, where preschool attendance from the age of three leads to positive outcomes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We now have enough full-day preschool places nationally for every resident child aged three and above.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We have also achieved our commitment of ensuring that 80% of preschoolers can have a place in a Government-supported preschool.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Our early childhood services will continue to remain affordable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: This will make out-of-pocket expenses for full-day childcare in an Anchor Operator preschool comparable to primary school and after-school care fees combined.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: With the revised Additional Subsidy income thresholds announced by the Prime Minister in his Budget speech, many families can expect to pay even lower fees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We will also increase income thresholds for all the subsidy tiers below to reflect changes in household incomes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: This will further improve affordability of preschools for more than 60,000 lower- and middle-income families with young children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Mr Kenneth Tiong suggested portable preschool subsidies and additional salary support for non-Government supported operators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Portable subsidies have been raised in Parliament before.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We have studied this and highlighted that this approach alone may lead to unintended consequences, such as fee increases without improvements in accessibility or quality, or preschools becoming overly commercial.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We have seen this initiative implemented in other countries, only to be withdrawn a few years later.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Instead of one single approach, we take a more holistic, multi-pronged approach.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We provide funding to rigorously selected operators to cap fees and to maintain quality.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We also provide basic and means-tested additional subsidies, so basic subsidies as well as additional means-tested subsidies, to parents to ensure affordability, with lower-income families paying less.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: CDAs help parents further offset post-subsidy fees at preschools of their choice.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: And our schemes have worked well with demonstrated success in our accessibility and affordability outcomes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: In the next bound, MSF will place greater emphasis on the quality of preschools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Today, I will share our vision for "Quality Preschools", where children play, learn and grow alongside their peers, and develop holistically with strong foundations for life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: To achieve this vision, we will journey with the sector to enhance preschool capabilities, improve programme and professional quality, foster stronger parent-preschool partnerships, and strengthen research and innovation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: First, for our children, we will cultivate a preschool environment where they can play, learn and grow at a pace suitable for them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We will cater to children of different needs and backgrounds by encouraging play and offering different ways for them to learn and to explore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: In my maiden Parliamentary speech, I highlighted the crucial role of play in children's learning and development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Play teaches children to share, to solve problems, to adapt to new situations, and to manage emotions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We introduced play-based pedagogies in our earliest curriculum more than a decade ago.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: In the next bound, we will take it further.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We will share across the entire sector best practices they have observed from the operators and intensify the application of play in everyday lessons to make learning more responsive to each child's needs and interests, and to help children enjoy both learning and their childhood.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Next, we recognise that every child has their own strengths and learning needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: International research demonstrates that when educators design lessons that offer children different ways to learn, it improves teaching quality and leads to better outcomes for our children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We are strengthening efforts to equip educators to support every child's development to help them reach their full potential.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: For our parents, we will enable stronger partnerships with their child’s educators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Parents play a crucial role in bridging our children's development across preschool and home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: From my preschool visits, the principals have shared that parents want to be involved in shaping their children’s development and learning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: However, they are unsure how to partner educators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: So, we will work with preschools to strengthen educator-parent partnerships through clearer role definitions and shared best practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Educators are at the heart of preschool education and critical for our children's holistic development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We care for their well-being and want to ensure that more support is given to our educators as mentioned by Mr Melvin Yong.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We will better equip educators through pre-service training and in-service continuous development to adapt to our evolving early childhood landscapes, as they apply more play-based learning and support different learning needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We also acknowledge the challenges that our preschool operators face – given the long hours they spend caring for our children, there is little time to engage in other tasks, such as lesson planning or relevant upskilling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Preschools also do not have school holidays unlike primary or secondary schools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We have been enhancing our educators' career proposition over the years and we remain committed to doing more to ensure they are well-supported.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: For our operators, we will provide more support to strengthen their daily operations and to enhance their programme quality.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Through new innovation seed funding and establishing baseline technology requirements, we will support preschools to adopt digital capabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We want to streamline routine tasks while facilitating better communication with parents and fostering stronger parent-preschool partnerships.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We will also want to encourage more operators to seek accreditation under the revised Singapore Preschool Accreditation Framework 2.0, rolled out last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: As preschools attain a higher banding that reflects better service provision, parents can be assured of better quality.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: They can look forward to these preschools, which offer an even more enriching environment, to cater to their children's needs and to allow them to flourish.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: ECDA will lead efforts and collaborate with research partners to stay updated on emerging research and assess and encourage adoption of effective teaching and learning practices to raise the overall profile of our early childhood landscape.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Our focus this year will be to engage and closely work with preschool operators, our educators, our operators and our parents to further develop our plans, as we strive to deliver this vision of quality preschools over the next five years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: MSF and ECDA will share more details when we are ready.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: I have spoken about the importance of starting strong and starting early.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: So, that brings me to my final point to ensure that our families are set for life – starting together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Many parents tell me that raising children is a full-time job, and since many parents have to continue to work, we are often stretched thin and this is where the broader community plays a crucial role in supporting our children's development and makes raising children a joyful experience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: These events were supported by over 780 volunteers and benefited more than half a million participants.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: So, my deepest appreciation goes out to all our volunteers who help make these events possible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: These events provide opportunities for local communities to come together to foster friendship, to build support, while teaching our children what books cannot teach them – to care for those people and everyone around us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Take 11-year-old Capella, who started volunteering with Families for Life because she wanted to accompany her mother.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: What began as family time has become something much deeper – Capella has become more confident, more empathetic and discovered her own passion for volunteering and helping others.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Their shared service not only supported other families; it deepened their own bond.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: This is the ripple effect we see when families volunteer together – creating meaningful family time while making a difference in our community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We all have a role to play in supporting families in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: The Taskforce has started its work by looking at the life-cycle of PwDs of different needs and identifying the pain points and gaps that they encounter in the current system.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We will review community pathways and healthcare support for them to stay engaged in the community for longer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We will see how to better support our caregivers, by designing the system with them and their PwDs as a dyad and we will review and keep services affordable for all.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: The Government stands ready to invest more to support PwDs and their families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: But an inclusive society also means reshaping our systems and attitudes to embrace all abilities, and empowering PwDs to pursue their aspirations, achieve their potential and participate as integral members of society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Chairman, next, please allow me to say a few words in Mandarin.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: (In Mandarin):   Building an inclusive society requires whole-of-Government coordination and participation and effort from the entire society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Therefore, we have established the inter-Ministerial Taskforce on Assurance for Families with Persons with Disabilities to explore how to better provide assistance to persons with disabilities and their families in areas, such as employment, community living and affordability of disability support services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: The taskforce will also examine encouraging corporates and community partners to provide more job opportunities and community support for persons with disabilities, as well as promote greater social inclusivity, so that they can also pursue their dreams, realise their potential and contribute to society in their own way.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: MSF firmly believes that family is the cornerstone of society, so we are committed to building a nation that can support Singaporeans in forming families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Marriage, parenthood – we support Singaporeans through various measures at every important stage of life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Worth mentioning is our progress in preschool education.
