speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Today, every child above three years old in Singapore can receive quality, affordable preschool education, and in the next phase, we will further enhance the quality of preschool education, continuing to give children a good start in life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, at MSF, families are at the heart of all we do.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Strong families need effort and they are built by entire communities working together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: The Government provides broad-based support to help families start strong, early and, together, setting firm foundations and giving every child a good start.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: For families who are more vulnerable, we offer a steady hand and a supported ladder, so that they too can climb and thrive on their own terms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: For families with PwDs, we are committed to removing barriers and working with the community to create opportunities that foster inclusion and belonging.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Over the past week, our House has shared our respective visions of a "we first" society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: For MSF, this vision comes alive when our social service sector, community and our corporates partner us to create better outcomes for families and individuals that we serve.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: By sharing in this commitment that "Better Starts with Us", each of us make the difference together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Let us work towards stronger families, stronger communities, a stronger Singapore.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: The first on the expansion of ComLink+ social health integration pilot.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: So, this is directed at Minister of State Zhulkarnain.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: How many more ComLink+ residents is MSF looking to bring onboard this expanded pilot and where, which ComLink+ towns is MSF looking to expand this pilot to?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: And also, will family coaches and public health institutions be sharing data to support clients to navigate the system and avoid the navigation, like Minister of State Zhulkarnain spoke about?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Second bucket of clarifications on the ComLink+ skills upgrading support pilot.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: I just wanted to ask if family coaches will be working with IHLs and the course providers to signpost clients to certain courses and also to help them to enrol and get on board these courses?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: A third bucket of clarifications on supporting our professionals in the sector to uplift them, even as they care and pour their heart and soul to care for clients.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Does MSF have plans to enhance the support to professionals for professional development and career advancement opportunities in the sector?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: On social health integration, we focus our efforts on the health issues that are most likely to disrupt the broader social goals.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Last year was the trial for the social health integration and about 500 families were involved.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: In terms of the data sharing, MSF works closely with MOH, and the health care clusters so the relevant health information, like the children's mandatory immunisation records would be shared via a system interface with the family coaches.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: The second bucket of questions on the skills upgrading scheme.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: We also engage the IHLs on their application, to help them with their application as well.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We work with the industry practitioners, including the training providers, education institutions, the professionals themselves and their associations, to put up what we call the skills framework for social service.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Within this framework, we lay out the competencies needed for the families of social sector jobs so that professionals know clearly what they need to have in order to articulate and for their career planning.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is very useful for both the trainers, training institutions as well as for the individuals and the associations.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They can study, even if they have a degree, of which they have to have one to practise as full professionals in this field – in alternate or related fields, for example, in psychology.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: But we want to also look at how we can expand these fields of studies that may not look as related as they were, maybe 10 years ago, but may be relevant today.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, AI, for example, how they can be related to their work in social service.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: There are also of course, short-term grants for individuals to look at, to take up the courses and then to uplift their ability and their skills.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Not necessarily to enhance their career possibilities, but also to support their clients better.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In the meantime, SSAs, too, should use this framework, because they may want to attract talents from outside who may not have the requisite professional degrees or qualifications to practise in this sector.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I see a number of hands, but guillotine time is 12.15 pm.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I have three clarifications for Minister of State Goh Pei Ming, they are all related to preschools.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: One, given the critical importance of quality early childhood education in shaping our children's developmental outcomes, how can ECDA further strengthen the capabilities of preschools to better engage parents as active partners in their children's learning and development?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Two, the Ministry of Education (MOE) has introduced a right to disconnect policy so that school teachers are not expected to respond to work matters after school hours.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Given that preschool educators also face demanding workloads, could the Minister of State clarify whether ECDA has similar safeguards for our preschool educators?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Three, recognising that continuous professional development is fundamental to maintaining high educational standards, what steps is ECDA taking to enable our early childhood educators to pursue meaningful professional development opportunities, for example, giving study awards or time off for the preschool educators?

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Mr Chairman, let me take the questions part by part.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: First in terms of how we will build stronger parent-preschool partnerships, we believe that this partnership is important to help bridge the overall development and learning of our children between the home and the preschool.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: They are not separate entities, that experience has to be collective.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Therefore, we want to see more parents participate in our preschools.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: In fact, one of my recent visits to My First Skool in Anchorvale, Sengkang, I was very encouraged, it was the day of the launch of the health screening and I observed there was a parent doing a storytelling exercise together with the children.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: After that I managed to speak to her and she was sharing with me that My First Skool, at least at that centre, regularly sends out messages, sharing what are the opportunities for excursions, for storytelling, participating in games, sports or even coming in for rather mundane activities.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: But these experiences allow for the parent as well as the child to have a common experience that goes beyond the classroom back into the living rooms, over the dining table, where they talk.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: And in fact, the parent also knows many of the names of the child's friends.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: I thought that was very precious, very, very meaningful, and we want to have more of such experiences.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: And for this parent, when she walked away, this was sometime about 9.45 am in the morning, I remember being quite encouraged that how come she was able to do this?

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: She told me she was going to work, so I guess some of the flexible work arrangements have also set in, and she is well supported by her employer in this regard.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: So, from ECDA's view, what we are hoping to do more, as I mentioned earlier, we want to talk to the preschools, share many of their best practices.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We understand within the landscape, it is a little bit varied.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We want to collate and promulgate many of these across.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We also want to perhaps set clearer expectations of what the educator is and is not supposed to do, what the parent is and is not supposed to do and also, perhaps in this process, enable digital capabilities to foster this partnership.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: The second part of the question on the right to disconnect and understanding that MOE has a similar policy.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Once we formalise this, will promulgate to all.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: But perhaps my own experience, I also have a preschooler in my home, but I do not have the phone numbers of the teachers, nor is it shared.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: I call the general office and through that, the messages get shared to the teachers when they need to.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: The third question pertains to how do we allow our educators to have meaningful professional development opportunities.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We recognise it is important for them to be well supported in their journey by ECDA, and to have time to attend to not just the professional but also their personal learning needs.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We have mechanisms, such as a Continuing Professional Development roadmap, whereby we help guide and mentor our educators through this journey in terms of what courses that they can attend to upgrade, to upskill, and many of these courses are provided by the National Institute of Early Childhood Development, as well as other training providers, so we allow them a certain scaffold for them to continue to grow and progress in their careers and, of course, with new pedagogies, we hope that they will stay current.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: A few months ago, I met a group of ECDA Fellows.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: They shared with me, and this is a group of very senior principals and educators, and they shared with me some of their feedback, so we are looking into it.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We are looking to offer more bite-sized continuous development opportunities.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We are also looking into how we can ease the workload, more non-contact time, ensuring there is protected time for professional development, time for reflection, time for individual planning and more importantly, at the end of the day, all these allow for the development of the educators, which translate into better development and teaching for our children, benefiting our future.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: If per-child funding is the right principle for allocating resources among Anchor Operator centres, then why is it the wrong principle for allocating resources among all licensed centres?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Number two, I thank Minister of State Goh for his emphasis on play-based learning.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Ms Loy Wee Mee, who I mentioned in my cut, is a – if not the expert – on play-based learning in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: So, does the Ministry acknowledge that their operator funding model is making the play-based learning expert's schools, and others like hers, unviable?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: And what is your message to the independent operators?

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: And that is also to encourage the centre to improve on quality to attract more parents to come to them, to provide better curriculum, and per child enrolment basis allows for that.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: However, that is a different conversation from resources for all centres, and I note that the Member has over past instances also raised that we should provide funding to be assigned to the child rather than to the centres.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: It goes back to the fundamental principle of how we build the early childhood sector.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We have done this, like I explained in my speech earlier, through various means or various funding approaches, both on the subsidy side to the preschools directly; on the demand side to the parents, as well as allowing the parents to have some free choice through the CDA.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We believe that the confluence of that allows us to achieve the balance and the right incentives for both the preschools' operators, as well as in terms of our support for the parents.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: One particular area that I would like to perhaps talk about is how do we run our anchor operator and partner operator schemes, because I think the point of the Member's question is how do we better support – there is a slice of operators that may not be getting Government funding.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: The operators must be both willing and capable to meet stringent scheme requirements, and these include the provision of affordable quality preschool services as well as the commitment to improve the professional development of their educators.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: There can be good reasons why certain operators are not part of the Anchor Operator or the Partner Operator schemes.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Some operators simply choose not to participate because of legitimate business considerations, such as they have already established a premium market positioning.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Others may be providing a very specialised, a very niche service or programme.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: They have higher business costs that may not justify for Government funding to go in.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: And to maintain the quality and sustainability of these programmes, they may also not believe and subscribe to the fee caps that we have imposed through our operator schemes.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Some preschools are also in areas with higher Permanent Resident and foreigner numbers, and therefore, Government support is less relevant.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Some operators may also not be selected because of the application process.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: The Partner Operator selection is competitive and factors, such as track record in delivering services, financial sustainability, accessibility of the centres as well as the local preschooler demand in the immediate area where the preschool is located.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: So, all those are factors that we consider, and we want to do so because we need to be judicious in how we spend Government money.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: I acknowledge the point the Member raised about Ms Loy.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: I think we will be keen to talk to her and see how she can help in the sector.

speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
text: Future care planning extends beyond employment and financial planning, and it includes residential arrangements, community access and the maintenance of social relationships.

speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
text: So, I would like to ask if the Ministry has or intends to help develop a playbook or have a coach or peer support system to guide family members involved in this future care planning process?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Indeed, future care planning, especially with the person, as well as the caregivers at the centre of this planning process, is absolutely essential.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: That is a key organising principle for service models moving forward.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Just want to highlight a few examples, so that we can illustrate the point.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I have mentioned briefly in my speech that the Enabling Skills for Life Programme, an important component, is the individual curriculum and development plan, for which the caregivers, as well as the PwD themselves are very intimately and closely involved in the creation of the content and the milestones within.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In yesterday's cuts, Ms Denise Phua, also talked about the Family Life Navigator Model, and she likened that to the ComLink model, where we have different families, different ranges of needs being supported by somewhat like a defender.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We totally agree with that mission and that vision.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: What we need is some time, in order for us to assemble the right manpower, with the right aptitude, the right capability and competencies to do this.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: But in terms of vision, we are well aligned.

speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
text: And are there sufficient counsellors to support this capacity increase?

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We are working with the various service providers to ensure that there is adequate staffing as capacity expands.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We want to make sure that we are expanding while not compromising quality.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: I think that must be the key principle that we are observing here.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: The timeline of 2030 actually allows us to work together with the providers to build up the capacity in sync, as demand grows, and that also allows us to work with the educational service providers to help raise up this capability.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: To maintain service quality, there are two key principles or two key prongs that we are going to do this by.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We will recruit professionals with relevant credentials and experience.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Especially in FAM centres, we do need our counsellors to be a lot more experienced, slightly more experienced than usual, to deal with more complex cases.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Those with social work and psychology qualifications also undergo additional training to ensure they have the necessary counselling skills.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: At the same time, FAM counsellors will receive ongoing clinical supervision to maintain professional standards and to support their ongoing development.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I just want to thank Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric, Minister of State Goh and the SG Enable MSF team for being really sincere and responsive all these years.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Number one is, I am glad that the Ministry has curated some more enabling skills courses, but there is a real urgency because there is a lot of disruption in the AI-driven automation space, and many of the jobs, blue and white collared included, are really at risk, and there is urgency to have more deliberate intentional effort in this.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Therefore, that is why I recommended the National Disability Job Redesign Resource/Fund.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I would like to hear the Senior Parliamentary Secretary's views on that, because there is an urgency and we cannot wait until all the reports are out.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The second one is: there is a strong need also for those with moderate to high needs and that it will take a while for DACs to come up, and also, they are also costly.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I wonder if there is a possibility of looking at a lighter version of the ESHs, so that these services can be developed at the local community centres or residents' committee, supporting grassroots efforts as well, because I know many of my colleagues really want to support these families as well.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Money is scarce and time is even more.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Are there any other initiatives with supervision that can be formalised across neighbourhoods, such as the Touch Young Arrows Children's programme?

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My second question is that I understand ComLink+ families become FSC cases during crisis and family coaches take a step back.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Will the Ministry consider allowing family coaches to continue journeying with the families on the context that in times of crisis, more hands-on-deck is needed, and trust and relationship built with coaches can be more pertinent in these moments?

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Third question, has the Ministry explored grants to support caregivers with entrepreneurial endeavours with PwDs that they are caring for initiatives, such as Junlefont and Bakes by Ben?

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They are both started by caregivers with children with special needs, and they continue to provide and allow the children to be meaningfully engaged, yet allowing income generation and flexibility.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Lastly, riding on Member Denise's points to reduce wait time in the pressure valve of DACs, has the Ministry considered pilot integrating Senior Care Centres and DAC for adults, since DAC residents are getting older, and I have also been a care staff in both settings, and care needs of toileting, feeding and cognitive engagement are similar in objectives.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: I will address the first few questions and Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua will cover the rest.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Member asked about the effectiveness of ComLink+ and our evaluation of the success.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: We continuously monitor ComLink+ and we receive feedback from families that we serve and of course, from the family coaches themselves, the SSOs and FSCs.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: We understand that some families may find it difficult, as I have mentioned in my speech, to meet some of these conditions despite their best efforts, so we are actually working with the families and the family coaches themselves on how to encourage the families to achieve those milestones.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: I also referenced that in my speech that we will continually finetune our approach as we have learned more insights.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: On the local efforts, these are complementary to our programs already in MSF.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Families may take advantage of all the programmes in the community.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Family coaches also themselves connect our ComLink+ families and their children to such activities.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: For instance, in Choa Chu Kang and Keat Hong where I serve, we have specific programmes during the holidays for music and pharmaceutical visits for lower-income families.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: But MSF also will be looking towards working and understanding the best practices all across Singapore, across towns and try to implement programs at the local level.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: And I do encourage all Members in this Chamber, if Members have partners on the ground, do come up with innovative programmes to engage our low-income families and their children.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Lastly, on the FSCs, Member asked on the situation when the case is referred to the FSC, whether the family coach can continue journeying with the family, he said "all hands-on-deck" would help.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: However, this only typically happens when there is a crisis that happens to the family, like domestic violence, there is a divorce.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: So, in that situation, the priority would always be to stabilise the families.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: And they will also build rapport with the family and, hopefully, build trust, and this also allows one caseworker to be the main touchpoint for each family, and integrate the different support in the community for that family, so that again, the navigational nightmare would be avoided and they have one touchpoint.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: DACs are actually meant to support PwDs with moderate to more severe needs and in fact, the profile of clients in DACs are actually rather young, with many of them coming straight from SPED schools.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The focus really is on equipping and getting these clients ready for independent living in the community, but we acknowledge his suggestion and we will take it back to take a closer look.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In fact, I have been supporting Jun Le.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: My two National Day Parade outfits for the past two years has been designed by Jun Le.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: And I thank Member Lee Hui Ying for also jumping onboard last National Day Parade.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: But that aside, we are already working with them.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, for instance, like as part of the i'mable collective, we have curated a whole host of home-based businesses, such as Jun Le, and Jun Le is featured as part of the i'mable collective as well.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Every year end, when we have our Enabling Lives Festival, we do have a marketplace where we feature each of these home-based businesses, like Jun Le themselves, and that is where I got to know designers like Jeremiah, we have Isaac and Sheng Jie, who is so good with the dinosaur drawings, and so on.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: And I really hope that Members of the Chamber, and also all of us out there – this is my call to all of you to also support these businesses.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: It is not just about buying a clay or porcelain dinosaur.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The act is not in the buying, but because that buying is living proof of their dignity, of their ability to also contribute to society and to be an upstanding member of society.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: And I behove all Members of the Chamber to also support these home-based businesses, because many of them, for instance, Bakes by Ben and his mum.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: They are not letting life get them down, and they are saying, "Look, I am playing my part", and in a way they are crying out to society to say, "Support us as well in this journey".

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I have come on board and I invite everyone to share in this journey.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Let us all support local talents and local businesses.

speaker: The Chairman
text: On that note, can I invite Mr Xie Yao Quan, if you would like to withdraw your amendment?
